CHOICE: 3
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 3 is the only one that handles the problem correctly. Solutions 1 and 2 rely on checking $A_5$ alone and then asserting that no other groups belong to $\mathcal{G}$, which is unjustified. Solution 3 covers the prime-power case through Manz's classification, which gives $A_5$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(8)$, and it identifies the $\omega=2$ family $A_7$, $S_7$, $3\cdot A_7$. I checked the $A_7$ and $S_7$ degree lists and both have every nonlinear degree with exactly two prime divisors, so those groups are in $\mathcal{G}$ and contribute 7. The $3\cdot A_7$ degrees and the claimed exclusion of other socles and of new primes in the solvable-radical analysis are not fully verified, so my confidence is moderate.
